body:
The bottle looked clean until it dried, when a green line appeared above the water. We had filled it after the field truck passed, at a tap on the other side of the road.

The next family along the road noticed the smell without seeing the truck. The bean leaves watered from that tap had turned dark and slick. I kept the bottle overnight to see if the line came back.
title: Diary page

body:
I covered the herbs when the patrol vehicle passed. It stopped at each gate and a man read names from a list; ours was not on it, and the neighbor's was crossed through.

I wrote down the day because of the count they gave us. We were told to keep quiet about it. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: Notebook page

body:
A driver stopped at our gate and read from a list before accepting a cup of tea. He asked us not to use the road past the barrier. The count on the list did not match the people in our house.

The child's blanket was drying nearby when they taped the gate. They told us to keep the tag and say nothing. I kept this separate because the person involved might come back for it.
title: Letter

body:
The workers removed their boots outside. By morning the pale dust had traveled inside on the dog’s paws. No one in the house had gone near the trial rows.

We washed the small cup twice and put it away from the others. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: Notepad page

body:
The sprayed rows by the orchard were still wet when I filled the sample jar. Its lid came loose in the grocery bag, and the table smelled of that bitter spray all evening.

The dog would not drink from the dish left outside. The pear leaves along the sprayed rows curled and went brown within two days.
title: Diary page

body:
We sprayed the lower field after the seed trial and the wind carried it over the water path. The bean rows beside the path are scorched in a long yellow streak.

I left the date on the page and did not smooth the torn edge. The leaves on the nearest rows are still curling.
title: Notebook page

body:
The calves refused their water. I poured it into a spare pail and found an oily rim once it settled, the same sheen as the puddles in the sprayed pasture. We draw from the same shallow well as the field.

The oats along that pasture have gone patchy and pale. I kept the pail aside from the others.
title: Letter

body:
The driver washed the sprayer beside the closed shop. He paid for soap but not for another bucket. The water ran through the drain toward houses that had no notice about the trial.

I wrote down the day because the first warning arrived after it. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: Notepad page

body:
The first rain after the field treatment left yellow flecks in a pan under the leak. The same flecks lay on the wheat leaves outside, thick along the rows we sprayed.

The child's blanket was drying nearby and held the same fine dust. I saved the pan because no one believed me when I described it.
title: Diary page

body:
The seed counter receipt lists a small charge for sample jars and a bag of the new treated seed. The corn I planted from it came up stunted and grey-streaked, while the old seed in the next row stands green.

We washed the small cup twice and put it away from the others. I wrote down the planting day beside the receipt.
title: Notebook page
